title: Most Roman doctors now reject predetermination: it destroys freedom and makes God the author of sin
source_text: XXVI. Sed multo major pars Doctorum Ecclesiae Romanae sententiam istam hodie rejicit, & pertendit influxum illum praemoventem & praedeterminantem voluntates hominum ad singulos ipsorum actus, humani arbitrii libertatem prorsus evertere; ac praeterea inde sequi Deum esse peccati authorem, ut qui, ex ista sententia, homines praedeterminet etiam ad actus intrinsece malos, & quandam male agendi necessitatem iis imponat.
pass_a_gloss: But by far the greater part of the Doctors of the Roman Church today rejects that opinion, and contends that that influence premoving and predetermining the wills of men to each of their acts, altogether overturns the liberty of human choice; and moreover that thence it follows that God is the author of sin, as one who, according to that opinion, predetermines men even to acts intrinsically evil, and imposes on them a certain necessity of acting ill.
pass_b_english: The great majority of the Roman Church's teachers, however, now reject this view. They argue that an influence premoving and predetermining human wills to each of their acts completely destroys the freedom of human choice.
They add that it would make God the author of sin, since on that view he predetermines people even to intrinsically evil acts and lays on them a kind of necessity to do wrong.

choices.why: Kept as the Thomist technical term; Le Blanc explains 'physical' as opposed to 'moral', not to 'supernatural'.
